name: Synthaven
description: A neuroactive compound that accelerates the integration of Synthetic Neural Tissue with organic nerve architecture by upregulating axonal growth factor receptors and promoting myelin analog deposition along SNT-organic junctions. Standard SNT integration without pharmaceutical support takes 8–14 weeks; Synthaven reduces this to 3–5 weeks. Helix markets it primarily to clinics performing SNT implantation, but it has found a wide secondary market.
effects: reduces integration ghosting and signal artifacts
promotes stable myelin analog sheath formation
side_effects: integration dreams — vivid, disorienting neural noise during sleep
brief synesthetic episodes as new pathways form
rare: runaway axonal growth causing unexpected sensory cross-wiring
emotional lability during week 2–3 of treatment course
duration: Treatment course: 3–5 weeks; individual dose active 18–24 hours
cultural_context: Anyone who's had SNT installed knows the integration period — the weeks of lag, ghost sensations, and neural static while your brain learns to talk to the new tissue. Synthaven cuts that misery in half. Tier 2 workers often go without it because the course is expensive and they can't miss work for the dreams. Tier 3 and above consider it standard aftercare. Some users describe the integration dreams as the most vivid experiences of their lives.
story_hooks: A batch of Synthaven has been contaminated with an accelerant that causes runaway axonal bonding — patients are developing unintended neural connections to their chrome, giving them access to signals they were never meant to receive.
A the Gray Zone fixer is offering Synthaven below cost, sourced from a medical shipment that went missing — but the courier it was taken from worked for someone who will come looking.

A character undergoing emergency SNT implantation can't afford Synthaven and must endure the full unassisted integration while still working a dangerous job — every week of neural static is a week they might make a fatal mistake.
